### `transport.collect` (::catalyst::transport::CollectOp)

_Receive the current round's reply._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `transport.collect` $session (`,` $dest^)? attr-dict `:` qualified(type($session))
              (`,` type($dest)^)? (`->` type($result)^)?
```

Receives the current round's reply in one of two forms: a value form that
returns it as a tensor `$result`, or a destination-passing form that writes
it into the `$dest` buffer. The buffer shape gives the expected reply size.

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{MemoryEffects::Write on ::mlir::SideEffects::DefaultResource}`

#### Operands:

| :-----: | ----------- |
| `session` | An opaque transport session handle, tagged with its role. |
| `dest` | 1D memref of 1-bit signless integer or 8-bit signless integer or 16-bit signless integer or 32-bit signless integer or 64-bit signless integer or index values |

#### Results:

| Result | Description |
| :----: | ----------- |
| `result` | 1D tensor of 1-bit signless integer or 8-bit signless integer or 16-bit signless integer or 32-bit signless integer or 64-bit signless integer or index values |

### `transport.create` (::catalyst::transport::CreateOp)

_Create a transport session for a role._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `transport.create` attr-dict `->` qualified(type($session))
```

Creates a session on the backend selected by `backend_lib` and `config`; the
result type's role picks controller or coprocessor. When `key` is set, the
session is registered under it so `transport.get_session` can resolve it from
another function.

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{MemoryEffects::Write on ::mlir::SideEffects::DefaultResource}`

### `transport.establish_channel` (::catalyst::transport::EstablishChannelOp)

_Arm the channel for the given transport._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `transport.establish_channel` $session $transport attr-dict `:` qualified(type($session))
```

Prepares the channel selected by `transport` for the rounds that follow.
Runs after `exchange_keys` and before `post`/`collect`.

### `transport.get_session` (::catalyst::transport::GetSessionOp)

_Resolve a session by role and key._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `transport.get_session` attr-dict `:` qualified(type($session))
```

Returns the session that `transport.create` registered under (role, `key`),
where the role is taken from the result type. Lets a session created in one
function be used in another without passing it as a value.

### `transport.reply_slot` (::catalyst::transport::ReplySlotOp)

_This round's slot in the transport-owned reply ring (controller)._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `transport.reply_slot` $session attr-dict `:` qualified(type($session)) `->` type($slot)
```

The peer writes its reply here. Handing this to `transport.collect`.
The slot is reused every ring wrap, so a consumer has to read it before the next round.

### `transport.set_coprocessor_fn` (::catalyst::transport::SetCoprocessorFnOp)

_Bind the function the coprocessor runs._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `transport.set_coprocessor_fn` $session attr-dict `:` qualified(type($session))
```

Binds the function the coprocessor applies to received messages before
replying. `symbol` is the name the coprocessor resolves and invokes; an
empty symbol selects a default.

Whether that function is invoked per message or once at start to launch a
persistent engine belongs to the backend. The runtime
binds through whichever of the two the backend implements.

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{MemoryEffects::Write on ::mlir::SideEffects::DefaultResource}`

#### Attributes:

</table>

| :-----: | ----------- |
| `session` | coprocessor transport session |

### `transport.stage_payload` (::catalyst::transport::StagePayloadOp)

_Stage a payload into this round's request slot (controller)._

Syntax:

```
operation ::= `transport.stage_payload` $session `,` $payload attr-dict `:` qualified(type($session)) `,` type($payload)
```

Writes through the backend, which knows how its slot memory has to be written.

`decoder_id` addresses the round at one of the peer's decoders. It travels in the frame
beside the payload, so it is staged with the payload rather than given to the send.

Interfaces: `MemoryEffectOpInterface (MemoryEffectOpInterface)`

Effects: `MemoryEffects::Effect{MemoryEffects::Write on ::mlir::SideEffects::DefaultResource}`

</table>
